models_evaluated: machine-learning regression and binary classification models predicting AzBio and CNC scores

links.outcome: Model sensitivity and PPV versus existing referral heuristics for CI candidacy
links.effect: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).
links.quote: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).

links.outcome: Effect of test-retest noise in predictor inputs on attainable model precision
links.effect: Variability analyses indicated that attainable precision is bounded by noise in key predictors.
links.quote: Variability analyses indicated that attainable precision is bounded by noise in key predictors.

unlisted_practices: Reformulating regression outputs into binary classification tasks using clinical thresholds to improve clinical utility

screen.reason: Evaluates practical lessons for clinical utility in predictive AI, specifically comparing operational threshold selection strategies and assessing the impact of input data variability/noise on model performance.

primary.practice: threshold selection aligned with clinical utility and input variability
